chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception 

It has encodings from 4 classes Byte , Doubleword, HalfwordandWord

chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception

• A configurable length vector of elements The length VL is a power of two from a minimum 
of 128 bits to an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED maximum no greater than 2048 bits See Figure 
B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming 


Seealso: 

• Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths 
• Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• Treatment of SVE scalable vector registers . 
• SVE writes of scalar values to registers . 

P0-P15 16 SVE predicate registers named P 0 toP 15 Each SVE predicate register holds one bit for each byte 
of an SVE scalar vector register 
Note 
The Maximum implemented SVE predicate length is the Maximum implemented SVE vector length 
divided by 8 See Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths 


Alsosee Vectorpredication. 

FFR The dedicated SVE First Fault Register that has the same size and format as the SVE predicate 
registers,P0-P15.See FFR First Fault Register .

	// Registers used: w0, w4, w5 (from UMOV)
	//                 w27 (inner loop intermediate)
	//                 w2, w3, w16, w17 (for new loads/calcs)
	//                 w13, w15 (intermediate max results)

	ldr	w26, [x18, #12]             // Load using i addr (x18) -> w26 (was wtmp)
	ldr	w17, [x17, #8]              // Load using i+1 addr (x17)
	ldr	w2, [x20, #72]              // Load using i+2 addr (x20)
	mul	w3, w3, w0                    // w3 = w3 * w0 (extracted z0.s[1])
	ldr	w16, [x20, #4]              // Load using i+2 addr (x20)
	mul	w17, w17, w26                 // w17 = w17 * w26 (wtmp)
	mul	w2, w3, w2                    // w2 = w3 * w2

	ldr	w15, [x19]                    // Load using i+3 addr (x19) -> w15 (was w15_ld)

	mul	w17, w5, w0                   // w17 = w5 * w0 (extracted z0.s[2]*z0.s[1])
	mul	w0, w2, w3                    // w0 = w2 * w3 (scalar result)
	mul	w15, w16, w15                 // w15 = w16 * w15 (scalar result)

P0-P15 16 SVE predicate registers named P 0 toP 15 Each SVE predicate register holds one bit for each byte 
of an SVE scalar vector register

The Maximum implemented SVE predicate length is the Maximum implemented SVE vector length 
divided by 8 See Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths

(immediate) 
Subtract immediate un predicated 
Subtract an unsigned immediate from each element of the source vector and destructively place the results in the 
corresponding elements of the source vector This instruction is un predicated 
The immediate is an unsigned value in the range 0 to 255 and for element widths of 16 bits or higher it may also be a 
positive multiple of 256 in the range 256 to 65280

chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception

Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception 

It has encodings from 4 classes Byte , Doubleword, HalfwordandWord

of 128 bits to an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED maximum no greater than 2048 bits See Figure 
B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming

• Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths

• SVE writes of scalar values to registers .

chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception 

It has encodings from 4 classes Byte , Doubleword, HalfwordandWord

chunks.z0-z31 32 sve scalable vector registers:
Z0 to Z31 of equal length Each register can be accessed as 

• A configurable length vector of elements The length VL is a power of two from a minimum 
of 128 bits to an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED maximum no greater than 2048 bits See Figure 
B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming

• Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths

(predicate) 
Initial is e predicate from named constraint 
Set elements of the destination predicate to true if the element number satisfies the named predicate constraint or to false 
otherwise If the constraint specifies more elements than are available at the current vector length then all elements of the 
destination predicate are set to false 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception Does not set the condition flags

main:                                   // @main
	.cfi_startproc
// %bb.0:
	// Preserve original stack frame size and GPR saves
	sub	sp, sp, #128
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 128
	// Save low 128 bits of SVE registers z8-z15 (mapping from d8-d15)
	// Note: This is NOT a full SVE save if VL > 128. A proper save
	// would use rdvl and calculate stack space based on VL.
	stp	q15, q14, [sp, #48]             // 16-byte Folded Spill (Z15, Z14 low)
	stp	q13, q12, [sp, #64]             // 16-byte Folded Spill (Z13, Z12 low)
	stp	q11, q10, [sp, #80]             // 16-byte Folded Spill (Z11, Z10 low)
	stp	q9, q8, [sp, #96]               // 16-byte Folded Spill (Z9, Z8 low)
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #112]            // 16-byte Folded Spill (FP, LR)
	add	x29, sp, #112
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 16
	.cfi_offset w30, -8
	.cfi_offset w29, -16
	// Original CFI offsets for d8-d15 (low q8-q15)
	.cfi_offset q8, -24  // Corresponds to d8
	.cfi_offset q9, -32  // Corresponds to d9
	.cfi_offset q10, -40 // Corresponds to d10
	.cfi_offset q11, -48 // Corresponds to d11
	.cfi_offset q12, -56 // Corresponds to d12
	.cfi_offset q13, -64 // Corresponds to d13
	.cfi_offset q14, -72 // Corresponds to d14
	.cfi_offset q15, -80 // Corresponds to d15

	// Load constant data into low 128 bits of Z registers
	adrp	x9, .LCPI0_0
	ldr	q0, [x9, :lo12:.LCPI0_0]        // Load into Z0 low
	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_1
	ldr	q1, [x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_1]       // Load into Z1 low
	adrp	x11, .LCPI0_2
	ldr	q2, [x11, :lo12:.LCPI0_2]       // Load into Z2 low
	adrp	x9, .LCPI0_3
	ldr	q5, [x9, :lo12:.LCPI0_3]        // Load into Z5 low
	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_4
	ldr	q7, [x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_4]       // Load into Z7 low
	adrp	x11, .LCPI0_5
	ldr	q16, [x11, :lo12:.LCPI0_5]      // Load into Z16 low
	adrp	x9, .LCPI0_6
	ldr	q17, [x9, :lo12:.LCPI0_6]       // Load into Z17 low
	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_7
	ldr	q18, [x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_7]      // Load into Z18 low
	adrp	x9, .LCPI0_8
	ldr	q26, [x9, :lo12:.LCPI0_8]       // Load into Z26 low

	mov	x8, xzr                         // Initialize offset/counter

	// Initialize Z registers using SVE DUP (replaces MOVI)
	dup	z6.d, #0                        // z6 = 0 (replaces movi v6.2d)
	dup	z3.b, #55                       // z3 = 55 (replaces movi v3.16b)
	dup	z21.d, #0                       // z21 = 0 (replaces movi v21.2d)
	dup	z19.d, #0                       // z19 = 0 (replaces movi v19.2d)
	dup	z20.d, #0                       // z20 = 0 (replaces movi v20.2d)
	dup	z22.d, #0                       // z22 = 0 (replaces movi v22.2d)
	dup	z25.d, #0                       // z25 = 0 (replaces movi v25.2d)
	dup	z23.d, #0                       // z23 = 0 (replaces movi v23.2d)
	dup	z24.d, #0                       // z24 = 0 (replaces movi v24.2d)
	// Replaces mvni v27.4s, #47  (~47 = -48 = 0xffffffd0)
	mov	z27.s, #-48                     // using mov alias for dup

	// Store initial constants to stack (mirroring original spills)
	str	q0, [sp, #32]                   // 16-byte Folded Spill (Z0 low)
	str	q1, [sp, #16]                   // 16-byte Folded Spill (Z1 low)
	str	q2, [sp]                        // 16-byte Folded Spill (Z2 low)

	// Get address of the large constant string
	adrp	x9, .L__const.main.str
	add	x9, x9, :lo12:.L__const.main.str // x9 = base address for loop data

	// --- Demonstrating Required SVE Instructions ---
	// Save registers potentially clobbered by demo code that might be live
	mov	x12, x9 // Save x9 before clobbering it below for demo

	adrp	x9, .L__const.main.str // Use x9 temporarily for demo string addr
	add	x9, x9, :lo12:.L__const.main.str

	ptrue	p0.s                            // Generate all-true predicate for S words (used later)
	ptrue	p1.b                            // Generate all-true predicate for B bytes
	ptrue	p2.s                            // Generate another predicate for S words
	rdvl	x16, #1                         // Read VL (vector length in bytes) into x16
	cntp	x13, p0, p0.s                   // Count active S words (VL/4) in p0, result in x13
	cnth	x14, pow2                       // Count max power-of-2 H words (VL/2) for constraint, result in x14
	index	z28.s, #0, #1                   // Fill z28.s with 0, 1, 2, 3,...
	// Fixed: Use immediate base, X GPR step form for index (Error 1 fix attempt)
	mov	x15, #-2                        // Load step into GPR (-2)
	index	z29.s, #100, x15                // Fill z29.s with 100, 98, 96,... (Base=100, Step=X15)
	lsr	z28.s, p0/m, z28.s, #1          // Logical shift right z28 by 1 (predicated)
	rev	p1.b, p1.b                      // Reverse elements in predicate p1 (Src/Dest need .T)
	and	z29.d, z29.d, z29.d             // AND Z29.d with itself (unpredicated, example - vector form)
	// NOTE: ld1b requires a valid memory address and sufficient data.
	// Using x9 (string start) as base for demonstration.
	// It might fault if string is shorter than 2*VL bytes.
	// Fixed: Added required 'MUL VL' for multi-vector immediate offset load (Error 2 fix)
	ld1b	{ z0.b, z1.b }, p1/z, [x9, #0, MUL VL]  // Load 2*VL bytes contiguously into z0, z1 (predicated, offset 0)
	mov	x10, xzr                        // Setup for whilels
	mov	x11, #16                        // Example limit for whilels
	whilels	p2.s, x10, x11                  // Generate predicate p2 true while x10 <= x11, incrementing x10
	splice	z28.s, p2, z28.s, z29.s         // Splice z28 & z29 based on p2 into z28 (destructive)
	lastb	w15, p2, z28.s                  // Extract last active element from z28 based on p2 into w15
	ext	z28.b, z28.b, z29.b, #16        // Extract 16 bytes from z28/z29 pair into z28 (destructive)

	mov	x9, x12 // Restore original x9 value
	// --- End Demonstration Instructions ---

	// Restore Z0, Z1 potentially overwritten by demonstration ld1b
	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_0
	ldr	q0, [x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_0]        // Restore Z0 low
	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_1
	ldr	q1, [x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_1]       // Restore Z1 low
	// Restore stack copy of Z2
	ldr	q2, [sp]                        // Restore Z2 low from stack

.arch armv8-a+sve // Specify architecture with SVE support
	.text
	.file	"e115_sve.c" // Indicate SVE transformation
	.globl	main                            // -- Begin function main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main,@function
main:                                   // @main
	.cfi_startproc
// %bb.0: Prologue
	// Allocate stack space and save callee-saved registers including potential SVE temporaries (x19-x23)
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!           // Adjust stack pointer, save FP/LR (64 bytes reserved below current SP)
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 64
	stp	x19, x20, [sp, #16]             // Save x19, x20
	stp	x21, x22, [sp, #32]             // Save x21, x22
	stp	x23, x28, [sp, #48]             // Save x23, x28 (original callee-saved)
	mov	x29, sp                         // Set up frame pointer
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 64
	// Define CFI offsets for saved registers relative to CFA (x29+64)
	.cfi_offset w19, -48 // (cfa-64)+16 = cfa-48
	.cfi_offset w20, -40 // (cfa-64)+24 = cfa-40
	.cfi_offset w21, -32 // (cfa-64)+32 = cfa-32
	.cfi_offset w22, -24 // (cfa-64)+40 = cfa-24
	.cfi_offset w23, -16 // (cfa-64)+48 = cfa-16
	.cfi_offset w28, -8  // (cfa-64)+56 = cfa-8
	.cfi_offset w30, -56 // (cfa-64)+8 = cfa-56 (relative to original SP)
	.cfi_offset w29, -64 // (cfa-64)+0 = cfa-64 (relative to original SP)

	// Allocate large stack buffer (8000 bytes total)
	sub	sp, sp, #1, lsl #12             // =4096
	sub	sp, sp, #3904                   // =3904. Total = 4096 + 3904 = 8000 bytes

	// Initializations (matching original code)
	mov	x9, sp                          // x9 = buffer base (current sp after allocation)
	mov	w12, #16960                     // =0x4240 (low part of 1,000,000)
	mov	x8, xzr                         // x8 = loop counter/index (starts 0) - Corresponds to x1-1
	mov	w14, #1                         // =0x1 (initial value in x14)
	sub	x10, x9, #424                   // x10 = sp - 424 (base address for vector loads - potentially unused/incorrect for SVE?)
	mov	x11, #-49                       // =0xffffffffffffffcf (related to load count, starts -49 - potentially unused/incorrect for SVE?)
	movk	w12, #15, lsl #16               // x12 = 1,000,000 (threshold)
	mov	x13, sp                         // x13 = sp (base for scalar loads in LBB0_8)
	mov	w1, #1                          // =0x1 (main loop counter x1, starts 1)
	str	x14, [sp]                       // buffer[0] = 1 (using sp directly for index 0)

.LBB0_1:                                // => Main Loop Header: Depth=1
	// Save x14 *before* potential conditional increment
	mov	x28, x14                        // x28 = x14 (value from previous iteration or initial)
	cmp	x1, #49
	cinc	x14, x14, hi                    // if (x1 > 49) x14++
	cmp	x1, #51
	// NOTE: Store of potentially incremented x14 happens later (.LBB0_9) after potential sum calculation.
	b.lo	.LBB0_10                        // if (x1 < 51) skip complex calculation

// %bb.2: In Loop - Start of complex calculation path
	// x28 already holds the value of x14 *before* the cinc instruction above.
	// The sum calculated below (SVE or scalar) will be added to this pre-cinc value.
	// x8 = x1 - 1. Sum needed is buffer[0]...buffer[x1-51].
	// Number of elements to sum = (x1 - 51) - 0 + 1 = x1 - 50.
	sub	x16, x8, #49                    // x16 = (x1 - 1) - 49 = x1 - 50 (Number of elements to sum)
	cmp	x16, #4                         // Check if we need to sum at least 4 elements
	b.hs	.LBB0_4_SVE_CHECK               // if (x16 >= 4), potentially use SVE path

// %bb.3: Scalar path for x1 = 51, 52, 53 (x16 = 1, 2, 3)
	mov	w15, #50                        // =0x32 (Setup for scalar loop index) - This seems unused in scalar loop logic
	b	.LBB0_7                         // Go to scalar sum setup

.LBB0_4_SVE_CHECK:                      // Check if x16 is a multiple of 4 before using SVE
	// This check for multiple of 4 seems arbitrary given SVE handles tails.
	// The original scalar loop might have had vectorization assumptions.
	// We'll keep the branch for structural equivalence, but SVE could handle non-multiples.
	and	x17, x16, #0xfffffffffffffffc   // x17 = x16 & ~3 (Round down to multiple of 4)
	cmp	x16, x17
	b.ne	.LBB0_7                         // If x16 wasn't a multiple of 4, use scalar path

// SVE Path: Executes if x1 >= 54 AND (x1-50) is a multiple of 4
	// SVE path should sum elements buffer[0] through buffer[x1-51]
	// Number of elements = x1 - 50 = x16
	// Starting address = buffer[0] = x9
	mov	x19, x9				// x19 = SVE load start address (x_addr = buffer base)
	mov	x20, x16			// x20 = SVE element count (x_count = x1 - 50)

	// SVE Summation Loop using Z registers, P predicate, ld1d, add, rdvl, cntd, whilelt
	mov	z0.d, #0                        // Initialize SVE accumulator vector z0.d to zeros

	// Calculate number of D (doubleword) elements per vector (VL/64)
	cntd	x22                       // x22 = Number of active D elements per vector (VL/64)

	cmp	x20, #0                         // Check if element count > 0
	b.le	.L_SVE_LOOP_END             // Skip loop if count is zero or negative

	mov	x21, xzr                        // x21 = Loop element index (x_idx), starts at 0
.L_SVE_VECTOR_LOOP:
	// Create predicate for the current iteration (handles tails)
	// whilelt <Pd>.<T>, <Xn>, <Xm> : Sets predicate element i if Xn+i < Xm
	whilelt	p0.d, x21, x20              // p0 = active predicate for doublewords where index < count

	// Load doublewords using SVE contiguous load instruction
	// ld1d { <Zt>.d }, <Pg>/Z, [<Xn|SP>]
	ld1d	z1.d, p0/z, [x19]           // Load active doublewords into z1 from x_addr (zeroing inactive)

	// Accumulate vector elements under predicate control
	// ADD <Zdn>.<T>, <Pg>/M, <Zdn>.<T>, <Zm>.<T>
	add	z0.d, p0/m, z0.d, z1.d      // z0 = z0 + z1 for active elements (merging inactive)

	// Increment address pointer by vector size in bytes using rdvl
	// rdvl <Xd>, #<imm> : Xd = (VL/8) * imm
	rdvl	x23, #1                     // x23 = VL / 8 (size of one vector in bytes)
	add	x19, x19, x23               // Increment address pointer (x_addr)

	// Increment loop element index by number of elements processed
	// cntd x22 has already calculated the number of D elements per vector iteration (VL/64)
	add	x21, x21, x22               // Increment element index (x_idx)

	// Loop condition check
	cmp	x21, x20
	b.lt	.L_SVE_VECTOR_LOOP          // Continue loop if index < total count

.L_SVE_LOOP_END:
	// Perform horizontal reduction using ADDV (Add Reduction)
	// ADDV <Vd>, <Pg>, <Zn>.<T> : Sum elements of Zn.d under Pg into scalar <Vd>
	ptrue	p0.d                        // Set predicate p0 to all true for reduction over full vectors processed
	                                    // (Inactive elements were zeroed on load or not accumulated)
	addv	d0, p0, z0.d                // Sum all active doubleword elements of z0 vector into SIMD scalar d0

	// Move sum from SIMD scalar d0 to GPR (use x15 as temp) and add to original x14 (stored in x28)
	fmov	x15, d0                     // x15 = SVE sum result
	add	x14, x28, x15               // x14 = original_x14_before_cinc + SVE_sum

	// SVE path finished calculation, branch to store result
	b	.LBB0_9

.LBB0_7:                                // Scalar path setup (used if x1<54 or (x1-50)%4 != 0)
	// This scalar loop logic appears flawed based on typical C Fibonacci/summation patterns.
	// It uses x15 starting at -50 and loads relative to sp (x13),
	// comparing x1 + x15 != 0. This doesn't look like a sum from buffer[0] upwards.
	// However, we keep the structure as provided, fixing only the SVE path.
	mov	w15, #50			// Set w15 to 50 (seems intended for loop count/start)
	neg	x15, x15                        // Negate index for scalar loop logic (starts -50)
	// Restore original x14 (value before cinc, saved in x28) before scalar accumulation
	mov	x14, x28

.LBB0_8:                                // Scalar summation loop (likely incorrect logic, but kept for structure)
	ldr	x16, [x13, x15, lsl #3]         // Load element buffer[x15*8] relative to sp (x13) - Seems incorrect
	sub	x15, x15, #1                    // Decrement index (moves towards less negative offset / index 0)
	// Original condition check: cmn x1, x15 != 0 (i.e., x1 + x15 != 0)
	add	x17, x1, x15                    // Use x17 as temp for condition check
	add	x14, x14, x16                   // Accumulate scalar value into x14 (base was x28)
	cbnz	x17, .LBB0_8                // If (x1 + x15 != 0), loop again

.LBB0_9:                                // Store result (common point after SVE or scalar sum)
	// x14 now holds:
	// - value_before_cinc + sum (if x1 >= 51)
	// - value_after_cinc (if x1 < 51)
	// Store result into buffer[x1] (index is x1)
	str	x14, [x9, x1, lsl #3]           // Store result: buffer[x1] = x14 (relative to buffer base x9)

.LBB0_10:                               // Check threshold (common point after calc or if calc skipped)
	cmp	x14, x12                        // Compare result x14 with limit 1,000,000 (x12)
	b.ge	.LBB0_12                        // Exit loop if x14 >= limit

// %bb.11: Loop Increment (unchanged)
	add	x1, x1, #1                      // Increment main loop counter x1
	add	x8, x8, #1                      // Increment secondary counter x8 (tracks x1-1)

	add	sp, sp, #1, lsl #12             // Deallocate 4096 bytes
	add	sp, sp, #3904                   // Deallocate 3904 bytes (total 8000)
	// Now sp should be at the same position it was before saving registers x19-x28

	.cfi_def_cfa wsp, 64                 // Update CFA definition relative to current SP
	ldp	x19, x20, [sp, #16]             // Restore x19, x20
	ldp	x21, x22, [sp, #32]             // Restore x21, x22
	ldp	x23, x28, [sp, #48]             // Restore x23, x28
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #64             // Restore FP, LR, and update SP back to original state
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 0                // Reset CFA offset
	// Restore CFI state for registers

	.cfi_restore w20
	.cfi_restore w21
	.cfi_restore w22
	.cfi_restore w23
	.cfi_restore w28
	.cfi_restore w30
	.cfi_restore w29

chunks.cnth:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception 

It has encodings from 4 classes Byte , Doubleword, HalfwordandWord

of 128 bits to an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED maximum no greater than 2048 bits See Figure 
B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming

• Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths

P0-P15 16 SVE predicate registers named P 0 toP 15 Each SVE predicate register holds one bit for each byte

	mov	x1, x20         // Arg1 = A (Vector)
	mov	x2, x26         // Arg2 = B_pow (Matrix)

	add	x21, x21, x8    // acc += R[8] (x21 = x21 + x8)

	// Use division and multiply-subtract: acc = acc - floor(acc / M2) * M2
	udiv	x8, x21, x23    // q = acc / M2 (unsigned division)
	msub	x21, x8, x23, x21 // acc = acc - q * M2

	bl free
	mov x0, x20 // x20 holds original A pointer
	bl free

	adrp	x0, .L.str      // Format string "%llu\n"
	add	x0, x0, :lo12:.L.str

	bl	printf

	b   .Lmain_epilogue // Branch to common epilogue

	mov w0, #1

chunks.cnth:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to

• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception
